migrations.summary: The product describes itself in one sentence: `description` in the `app` object of `src/app.config.ts`.
migrations.instructions: The release's `app/layout.tsx` shows `app.description` as the document's description — the line a search engine and a link preview put under the name — where it used to write a sentence of the template's own. `src/app.config.ts` is yours and an update does not touch it, so the key is missing there until you add it. Add `description: '<one sentence about your product>',` to the `app` object beside `name`. A project that keeps its own `app/layout.tsx` needs the key all the same, because the layout a project brings over from the release reads it.

migrations.summary: A route that answers an error or draws the not-found screen fails every browser suite unless it is declared in missingRoutes.
migrations.instructions: The audit, the presses, the keyboard walk, the vitals and `scripts/shot.ts` now read what a route answered: one that answered an error status or draws the not-found screen (`[data-missing-page]`) was measured as that screen and not as the route, so it fails. In `scripts/verify.config.ts`, which is yours, move every entry of `detailRoutes` that names a record that does not exist (the sample's `/requests/req_missing` and `/customers/missing`) into a new `missingRoutes` list; each must be the not-found screen, and one that renders a page fails. A not-found screen of your own carries `data-missing-page` on its root, as `MissingPage` does: inside a streamed shell a missing record has already answered 200.

migrations.summary: Meridian's faces ship with the release under `src/styles/fonts/`: a build loads them from there and fetches nothing from Google Fonts.
migrations.instructions: Your `app/layout.tsx` is yours, so an update does not touch it, and yours hands `--font-face-sans` and `--font-face-mono` their faces through `next/font/google`, which `next build` fetches from fonts.googleapis.com: with that host unreachable and no build cache, the build fails (`Build error occurred`). The update has delivered the two faces, `src/styles/fonts/Geist-Variable.woff2` and `src/styles/fonts/GeistMono-Variable.woff2`, with their licence. In the layout, replace the `next/font/google` import with `import localFont from 'next/font/local';` and each face's call with `localFont({ src: '../src/styles/fonts/Geist-Variable.woff2', weight: '100 900', variable: '--font-face-sans', display: 'swap' })` and `localFont({ src: '../src/styles/fonts/GeistMono-Variable.woff2', weight: '100 900', variable: '--font-face-mono', display: 'swap' })`, keeping the class names on `<html>` as they are. A layout that gives the tokens faces of its own from Google Fonts is the same case: ship the files and load them with `next/font/local`.
